meta.title: The 50-Mile Strip Where You Can Get Away With Murder #shorts
meta.description:
Imagine standing in a beautiful, remote corner of Yellowstone National Park, knowing you could commit the perfect crime and walk away completely free. There is a fifty-square-mile strip of land in Idaho, inside the park, known as the Zone of Death. Because of a bizarre loophole in the US Constitution, a jury cannot be legally formed here. The sixth amendment says you have a right to a jury from the state and district where the crime happened. But this district is federal, and literally zero people live in this specific Idaho sliver. No people means no jury, which means no trial. Congress has known about this terrifying legal glitch for years, but they still haven't fixed it. Would you ever dare to camp alone in this lawless zone? Hit follow for more mind-bending facts.
